text: Reading Correspondence tests how well you understand a message and its reply. Try this original CELPIP Reading Part 1 practice test as an untimed learning exercise. Read the email and answer six comprehension questions. Then choose words for five blanks in the reply. All 11 answers include explanations. This example is free to read without an account and is separate from our scored practice sets.
How to approach Reading Part 1

Start with the relationship and purpose. Who is writing, who will reply, and what decision or action does the writer need? A polite opening alone does not tell you the purpose.
Track changes carefully. Mark the original arrangement and the new one separately. Words such as instead, still and only often decide which detail answers a question.
Prove each comprehension answer with the message. The correct choice may paraphrase a sentence; an option that repeats a word can still change its meaning.
For the reply, use both messages. Read each completed sentence aloud in your head. Check the facts, the grammar and the writer’s tone before choosing.
Email: a change to the bicycle repair workshop
Subject: Saturday workshop — new meeting point
Hi Maya,

Thanks for offering to help at our bicycle repair workshop this Saturday. I had planned to hold it in the courtyard behind the community centre, but the forecast now shows steady rain. We have booked the centre’s ground-floor activity room instead. The workshop will still run from 10 a.m. to noon. Please arrive at 9:30 so we can lay protective mats under the repair stands before the participants come in.

We have twelve registrations, one for each bicycle workstation in the room. Registration is now closed, so please do not invite additional participants. Two people have asked whether they can bring children. I told them that each registered participant may bring one child, provided the child stays beside them. This exception does not create places for more bicycles. We are keeping the session small so everyone has time to practise.

The centre has a set of basic tools we can borrow, so you do not need to bring your own. However, its pump does not fit every tyre valve. Could you bring the small pump you used at our last event? We will cover punctures and brake checks, but we will not work on electric bicycles because neither of us has training in their electrical systems. Please remind anyone who asks that this is a learning session, not a full repair service.

I have already emailed the participants about the room change. Could you put a sign at the courtyard gate when you arrive? People who miss the email may still head there. Use the side entrance to bring in your bicycle; the main doors will be locked until 10. Let me know by Thursday evening whether you can still help. If the earlier arrival is a problem, I can ask Leo to set up with me.
Thanks again, Priya
Maya’s reply: choose an option for blanks 7–11
Hi Priya,
Thanks for the update. Moving the workshop indoors sounds [7] given the weather forecast. I can still help, but my bus does not arrive until 9:45. Please ask Leo to [8] before I get there.

I will bring my pump, but I will leave my basic tools at home because we can [9]. I will use the side entrance and put up the sign to [10]. My neighbour asked whether you could fix her electric bicycle; I will explain that it is [11].
See you on Saturday, Maya
Questions and answer explanations
Choose an answer before opening its explanation. For blanks, insert the complete option into the message. This learning exercise does not calculate an official CELPIP score.
1. Why is Priya writing to Maya?

To cancel Saturday’s workshop.
To explain changed arrangements and confirm Maya’s help.
To ask Maya to lead an electrical repair class.
To invite Maya to register as a participant.
2. Which part of the original plan stays the same?

The location in the courtyard.
The maximum number of registrations remaining available.
The workshop’s 10 a.m. start.
The use of the main entrance before setup.
3. What does Priya allow registered participants to do?

Bring one child who stays beside them.
Invite another adult to repair a bicycle.
Register an extra bicycle on arrival.
Leave children at a separate supervised activity.
4. Why does Priya ask Maya to bring her pump?

The centre has no tools at all.
Maya is expected to give it to the centre permanently.
The pump is needed to repair electrical systems.
The centre’s pump is not suitable for every tyre valve.
5. What is the purpose of the sign at the courtyard gate?

To announce that registration has reopened.
To direct participants who have not seen the email to the new room.
To tell volunteers that the workshop starts at 9:30.
To advertise a full bicycle repair service.
6. What does Priya’s offer to ask Leo show?

She no longer wants Maya to attend.
She plans to postpone the workshop if Maya is late.
She can arrange different setup help if Maya cannot arrive early.
She expects Leo to repair electric bicycles.
7. Choose the best option for blank 7.

sensible
unnecessary
impossible
disappointing because of the sunshine
8. Choose the best option for blank 8.

cancel the registrations
lock the side entrance
change the workshop to 9:45
help with the setup
9. Choose the best option for blank 9.

ask each child to supply them
borrow the centre’s set
buy them from Leo
repair bicycles without any
10. Choose the best option for blank 10.

invite more people to join
keep all children outside
help people find the new location
tell everyone to return on Thursday
11. Choose the best option for blank 11.

outside the scope of this workshop
the main topic of the session
welcome if she arrives before 9:30
included as a full repair service
Turn your mistakes into a reading strategy

Sort mistakes into changed details, permissions, purpose and reply context. For example, volunteers are asked to arrive at 9:30. Maya’s bus arrives at 9:45. The workshop starts at 10 a.m. All three times are real details, but only one answers question 2. For each reply blank, point to the fact in Priya’s email that makes the choice fit. Getting 11 out of 11 here does not establish an official CELPIP level. It shows how you handled this one untimed example.

Keep a short error log: your choice, the correct choice, the sentence or table cell that proves it, and the trap you missed. Then try a fresh question set to practise the same skill without relying on memory.
What should you practise next?

Use the free CELPIP Reading course for guided lessons, or download the free four-skill prep pack for printable practice. When you are ready to work under a clock, take a full CELPIP Reading practice test.
